title: Colimits of Cartesian Grothendieck diagrams inverting transport arrows
statement:
Use quasicategories, ordinary nerves, coherent diagrams, equivalence edges, mapping spaces and colimits in fixed containing universes as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $B$ be a small ordinary category and $U:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a strict functor to small ordinary categories. Define $E$ to have objects $(b,x)$ with $x\in U(b)$ and arrows $(b,x)\to(c,y)$ the pairs $(f,u)$ with $f:b\to c$ and $u:x\to U(f)y$. Composition is $(g,v)(f,u)=(gf,U(f)(v)u)$. For $f:b\to c$ and $y\in U(c)$ call $(f,1):(b,U(f)y)\to(c,y)$ a transport arrow. Let $H:N(E)\to\mathcal C$ be a coherent diagram in a quasicategory sending every transport arrow to an equivalence, and put $H_b=H|_{N(U(b))}$. Suppose every $L_b=\operatorname{colim}_{N(U(b))}H_b$ exists. These fiber colimits form a coherent diagram $L:N(B)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$: for $f:b\to c$, its map $L_c\to L_b$ is the composite
$$L_c\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{colim}_{N(U(c))}(H_b\circ N(U(f)))\longrightarrow L_b,$$
where the first arrow is the inverse of the colimit of the equivalence $H_b\circ N(U(f))\to H_c$ supplied by the transport arrows, and the second is reindexing along $U(f)$. If $\operatorname{colim}_{N(B)^{\mathrm{op}}}L$ exists, then $\operatorname{colim}_{N(E)}H$ exists and there is a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{colim}_{N(B)^{\mathrm{op}}}L\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{N(E)}H.$$
Under this equivalence each map $L_b\to\operatorname{colim}L$ is the comparison induced by the fiber inclusion $U(b)\to E$. The equivalence is an equivalence of colimit cocones, natural in $H$, and includes compatibility with any specified coherent cocone from $H$ to a fixed object. No nonemptiness condition on the base or its fibers is imposed; an empty fiber requires an initial object.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp. 4-5: Cartesian total category localized at transport arrows, then decomposition of a colimit-indexing category. The displayed transition formula is the ordinary-base specialization, with the existence-only refinement from the colimit universal property; source read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent-colimit result.

proof.text: Put $J=N(B)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Work in a universe containing $\mathcal C$, its functor categories and their mapping spaces; no local-smallness bound in the original smaller universe is needed. First check that the projection $p:N(E)\to N(B)$ is a split Cartesian fibration: for a lift $(f,1):(b,U(f)y)\to(c,y)$ and a map $(h,w):(a,z)\to(c,y)$ with $h=fk$, its unique factorization over $k$ is $(k,w):(a,z)\to(b,U(f)y)$. This is compatible with composition because $U$ is strict. Inner horns of ordinary nerves fill by composition, and this unique factorization fills the Cartesian outer horns in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. An arrow $(f,u)$ is Cartesian exactly when its vertical factor $(1,u)$ is an isomorphism: one direction follows by composing the chosen lift with a vertical isomorphism; in the other direction compare the two Cartesian factorizations over $f$ to obtain mutually inverse vertical maps. Let $F:J\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ be the functor classifying $p$, supplied by the opposite of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Its fiber-and-transport clause gives equivalences $F(b)\simeq N(U(b))$ with the simplicial fiber, and identifies $F(f)$ with Cartesian transport, which the chosen lifts $(f,1)$ realize as $N(U(f))$. The coherent classifying functor is supplied by this theorem; the chosen lifts identify its transport values, without a strict simplex-wise identification.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text: Thus $H$ inverts all Cartesian arrows, since it inverts the chosen lifts and takes ordinary isomorphisms to equivalences. Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-colimit-localization] to obtain $A=\operatorname{colim}_J F$ and $\ell:N(E)\to A$, with restriction equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{Cart}(p)}(N(E),\mathcal C)$. In particular $H$ extends to $\widetilde H:A\to\mathcal C$, with its specified equivalence on restriction. The restriction of $\ell$ to each fiber is the corresponding leg $i_b:F(b)\to A$. Applying the base-change clause $c_u\ell_{p_u}\simeq\ell_pr$ of [lem-coef-cartesian-colimit-localization] to $u=f:\Delta^1\to N(B)$ shows that the equivalence $i_c\simeq i_b\circ F(f)$ of colimit legs is, after applying $\ell$, the image of the Cartesian arrows $(f,1)$; hence the corresponding equivalence of restrictions of $\widetilde H$ has components $H(f,1)$.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text:
Restriction along the $i_b$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)$ with the limit, indexed by $N(B)$, of $D_b=\operatorname{Fun}(F(b),\mathcal C)$, whose transition along $f:b\to c$ is $R_f=(-)\circ F(f):D_b\to D_c$, identified with $(-)\circ N(U(f))$ by step 1. To verify the full functor-category assertion, use the Cartesian closed structure of [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout]. For every test infinity category $X$, currying and the defining mapping-space property of the Cat-infinity colimit give
$$\operatorname{Map}(X,\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C))\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal C))\simeq\lim_{b\in N(B)}\operatorname{Map}(F(b),\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal C))\simeq\lim_{b\in N(B)}\operatorname{Map}(X,D_b).$$
The equivalences are the actual restriction maps. The limit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] proves the claimed limit cone. Under it $\widetilde H$ is the compatible family $H_b$ with equivalences $e_f:R_fH_b\simeq H_c$ induced by $H(f,1)$, as shown at the end of step 2; their higher coherence data are those of the limit cone, and no strict identification with chains of transport arrows is needed. The constant functor at $T$ corresponds to the compatible constant families $\Delta_{F(b)}T$.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text:
For every $b$ and $T\in\mathcal C$ put $Q_b(T)=\operatorname{Map}_{D_b}(H_b,\Delta_{F(b)}T)$. These form a coherent functor $Q:N(B)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal S)$: for $f:b\to c$, restrict a cocone along $U(f)$ and then precompose with $e_f^{-1}$, giving
$$Q_b(T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{D_c}(R_fH_b,\Delta T)\xrightarrow{(e_f^{-1})^*}Q_c(T).$$
This construction uses the coherent mapping bifunctor of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], in a containing universe. The full coherent diagram in this construction is the mapping-space diagram of the two compatible objects $\widetilde H$ and $\Delta T$ in the limit from step 3, supplied by the final general clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-homotopy-descent]. That clause applies because $B$ is a small ordinary category and the restriction cone is limiting. Its transition along $f$ first applies $R_f$ on both mapping-space inputs and then identifies the source using $e_f^{-1}$; the constant target has its identity identification. Thus it gives precisely the displayed maps, with the higher simplices from the coherent cone. The mapping bifunctor makes this construction natural in $T$ and in parameterized transformations of $H$. We therefore use a coherent diagram already supplied by the mapping-space-in-a-limit theorem, rather than choosing inverse edges independently.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text: The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied to the colimit cocone $\lambda_b:H_b\to\Delta L_b$, gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L_b,T)\to Q_b(T)$, $a\mapsto\Delta(a)\lambda_b$, natural in $T$; hence $Q_b\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L_b,-)$. Apply the fully faithful Yoneda assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, identifying $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(-,L_b)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L_b,-)$. Every $Q_b$ lies in this Yoneda functor's full essential image. The inverse supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] therefore sends the whole coherent $Q$ to a functor $N(B)\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, equivalently $L:J\to\mathcal C$. The resulting equivalence of representing functors retains the chosen fiber colimit cocones; this constructs the full coherent $L$, not only its edge maps.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text: We identify the arrows of $L$, including their direction. Write $\lambda_b:H_b\to\Delta L_b$ for its representing cocone. The map of representing functors $Q_b\to Q_c$ sends $\lambda_b$ to the cocone $H_c\xrightarrow{e_f^{-1}}R_fH_b\xrightarrow{R_f\lambda_b}\Delta L_b$. By the dual evaluation equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], a transformation $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L_b,-)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L_c,-)$ is determined, up to a contractible space of choices, by its value on $1_{L_b}$, and has components $a\mapsto a\circ(\text{that value})$. Transporting along the representing equivalences, $L(f^{\mathrm{op}}):L_c\to L_b$ is the map corresponding to that cocone. Applying the same colimit universal property to the equivalence $e_f$ says that $\operatorname{colim}(R_fH_b)$ exists and its induced map to $L_c$ is an equivalence: a cocone on either of these equivalent diagrams corresponds, with its apex fixed, to a cocone on the other, so its initial cocone transfers. The map to $L_b$ is induced by $R_f\lambda_b$, namely reindexing along $U(f)$. Consequently $L(f^{\mathrm{op}})$ is the composite $L_c\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{colim}_{F(c)}(R_fH_b)\to L_b$, with the first arrow inverse to the equivalence induced by $e_f$ and the second induced by $R_f\lambda_b$. This also explains why no hypothesis that $U(f)$ is final, or preserves colimits, is needed.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text:
For each test $T$, the localization equivalence in step 2 identifies the space of cocones on $H$ with apex $T$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)}(\widetilde H,\Delta_A T)$. It applies to this pair because both $H$ and the constant diagram invert Cartesian arrows and the subcategory is full, so it retains all transformations. Apply the final general clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-homotopy-descent], which explicitly states the mapping-space formula for a limit of categories indexed by a small ordinary category, to the limit cone of step 3 and the ordinary category $B$. It gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(E),\mathcal C)}(H,\Delta T)\simeq\lim_{b\in N(B)}Q_b(T)\simeq\lim_{b\in N(B)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L_b,T).$$
The transition maps in the first limit are exactly restriction and $(e_f^{-1})^*$, since these are the gluing equivalences of its two limit objects; thus the second equivalence is an equivalence of diagrams, not merely of their values. All comparisons are natural in $T$. Only the generic mapping-space clause of the cited descent node is used; no choice of a model category $\mathcal A$ or a presheaf model for $\mathcal C$ is made.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text:
Let $M=\operatorname{colim}_J L$, which exists by the remaining hypothesis. Its actual colimit cocone $\mu_b:L_b\to M$, together with [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(M,T)$ with the last limit in step 7. Composing with the inverse equivalence there gives a natural equivalence
$$\Phi_T:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(M,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(E),\mathcal C)}(H,\Delta T).$$
Take $\gamma=\Phi_M(1_M)$, a specified coherent cocone $H\to\Delta M$. The dual evaluation equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], applied to the corepresentable $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(M,-)$ and $Q=\operatorname{Map}(H,\Delta-)$, says that the components of $\Phi$ are homotopic, coherently in $T$ and in parameters, to $a\mapsto\Delta(a)\gamma$. The dual cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $\gamma$ colimiting. Its restriction to the $b$-fiber is $\mu_b\lambda_b$ by the projection to $Q_b(M)$ in step 7. Thus $M$ is the required total colimit and its fiber comparison is the stated leg $L_b\to M$. This proves existence of the total colimit without assuming other colimits in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Peng Du, Reshaping limit diagrams and cofinality in higher category theory, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4(1), printed pp.4-5; agent mapping-space expansion with only the stated colimits.

proof.text: The construction is natural in $H$ and retains a specified cocone to any $T_0$. Indeed restriction, the localization equivalence, and the mapping bifunctor in steps 1-7 apply to parameterized transformations as well as objects. If $\mathcal H$ is the full functor subcategory of admissible $H$ with the assumed fiber colimits, the same $Q$ construction has parameters $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{op}}\times N(B)$. The fixed coherent inverse of the full Yoneda essential image in step 5 applies to this whole parameter category, giving $L$ functorially in $H$. Let $\mathcal H_0\subseteq\mathcal H$ be the full subcategory of those $H$ for which the constructed $L$ also admits its outer colimit. Step 8 gives the total colimit for every object of $\mathcal H_0$. Apply the dual universal-arrow assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to the constant-diagram functors, on their full subcategories of diagrams admitting the respective colimits, and restrict the resulting functors to $\mathcal H_0$. This makes both existing colimits functorial on precisely the common domain required by the hypotheses, together with their cocones. The equivalences $\Phi$ are their cocone-restriction comparison, so yield a natural equivalence of these colimit cocones. Equivalently, the colimit-cocone uniqueness in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies any chosen total colimit with $(M,\gamma)$, with a contractible space of cocone-preserving choices. A specified $H\to\Delta T_0$ corresponds under $\Phi_{T_0}^{-1}$ to its unique compatible map $M\to T_0$, so it is preserved, including its specified compatibility homotopies. For $B=\varnothing$, also $E=\varnothing$, and the assumed outer colimit is the initial object, as required. For $U(b)=\varnothing$, $Q_b(T)$ is contractible and the representing $L_b$ is initial; all formulas still apply. For $B$ terminal the formula is the identity fiber colimit. None of the steps requires a nonempty base or fiber.
